idiom_name: traits and self-types (roles as mixins) with a per-core role map; Selectable for dynamic lookup
implementation_notes: Scala expresses the role's 'specialization of its core' relationship with traits and self-types (`trait BorrowerRole { this: Customer => }`) and inherits the forwarding and composition machinery from mixin composition, including stackable traits (abstract override) for roles that decorate core operations; the compiler resolves abstract members across mixed traits, so the classic ComponentRole boilerplate disappears. Because mixins are fixed at construction, runtime add/remove still needs a role map on the core, or a Dynamic/Selectable wrapper whose reflective member lookup exposes role operations behind a uniform protocol. Use explicit role classes when roles need independent lifecycle or persistence; use mixin composition when the role set is closed at construction.
pitfalls: Mixin composition is fixed at construction and linearization order decides which stacked trait wins; runtime add/remove needs the role map.
Reflective dynamic member lookup (Dynamic/Selectable, structural types) costs performance and fails at runtime on typos - keep role lookup explicit at boundaries.
Class[?] keys erase type parameters, so the role identity must come from the specification key, not from the map's value type.
